quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the person who teaches your class every day!
quests.question: Teacher
quests.hint: You raise your hand when you have a question for this person.
quests.explanation: That's right! A teacher explains new lessons and answers our questions.
quests.funFact: Teachers often spend extra time planning fun lessons for their whole class!

quests.instruction: Touch the colorful stick we use to draw bright, colorful pictures!
quests.question: Crayon
quests.hint: It can melt if it gets too warm in the sun.
quests.explanation: Yes! A crayon is the waxy stick we use to color our pictures.
quests.funFact: One box of crayons can have more than sixty different colors inside!

quests.instruction: Touch the container we pack with food to eat at school!
quests.question: Lunchbox
quests.hint: It keeps your food safe on the way to school.
quests.explanation: That's right! We open a lunchbox at lunchtime to enjoy our food.
quests.funFact: Some lunchboxes have special cool packs inside to keep food fresh and cold!

quests.instruction: Find the item that comes in a big stack, ready for writing!
quests.question: Paper
quests.hint: You can fold it, cut it, or draw on it in class.
quests.explanation: Well done! Paper is ready for a pencil, crayon, or marker to color it.
quests.funFact: Most paper today is made from trees that are grown just for that purpose!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the room where your class learns together!
quests.question: Classroom
quests.hint: Your teacher and your classmates spend most of the day here with you.
quests.explanation: That's right! A classroom has desks, chairs, and a board for lessons.
quests.funFact: Classrooms around the world can look very different, but they are all places to learn!

quests.instruction: Point to the sticky roll that fixes a book with a torn page!
quests.question: Tape
quests.hint: It comes on a roll, and one side is very sticky.
quests.explanation: Yes! Tape is the sticky roll we use to join paper together.
quests.funFact: Some tape is clear, so you can barely see it once it's stuck down!

quests.instruction: Find the person who helps students learn to read, write, and count!
quests.question: Teacher
quests.hint: This person helps you learn new things and checks your work.
quests.explanation: Well done! A teacher guides the whole class through every lesson.
quests.funFact: A single teacher can help hundreds of students learn over many years!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool that keeps our lines from going wobbly!
quests.question: Ruler
quests.hint: It helps your lines look perfectly straight, never wobbly.
quests.explanation: Correct! A ruler stops our lines from turning out crooked.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people used their own feet and hands to measure things before rulers!

quests.instruction: Point to the seat every student has next to their desk!
quests.question: Chair
quests.hint: You pull it out before you sit down at your desk.
quests.explanation: Correct! A chair and a desk almost always sit right next to each other.
quests.funFact: Some classroom chairs are stacked together and stored when they're not needed!

quests.instruction: Point to the object that tells us it's almost time to go home!
quests.question: Clock
quests.hint: It has a round face, numbers, and hands that slowly move.
quests.explanation: Yes! A clock shows us the time with numbers and moving hands.
quests.funFact: Some classroom clocks have a big hand for minutes and a small hand for hours!

quests.instruction: Touch the flat holder that keeps our loose papers from getting lost!
quests.question: Folder
quests.hint: It has no pages of its own, but it holds other papers inside.
quests.explanation: That's right! We slide our worksheets into a folder to keep them tidy.
quests.funFact: Some folders have pockets on both sides to sort different papers!

quests.instruction: Point to the board that becomes clean again with just one wipe!
quests.question: Whiteboard
quests.hint: It hangs at the front of the classroom for everyone to see.
quests.explanation: Yes! A whiteboard is the smooth board where a teacher writes each lesson.
quests.funFact: Some whiteboards are magnetic, so little magnets can stick to them too!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool that cleans up pencil marks so you can try again!
quests.question: Eraser
quests.hint: It is soft and a little bit stretchy in your hand.
quests.explanation: Yes! An eraser rubs pencil marks off your paper so you can try again.
quests.funFact: Erasers are made from rubber, which is why they can bend and squish!

quests.instruction: Point to the flat surface where a student sits down to work!
quests.question: Desk
quests.hint: A chair usually sits right beside it, ready for you to sit down.
quests.explanation: Correct! A desk is where a student's books and pencils usually sit.
quests.funFact: The word desk comes from an old word meaning a table for writing!

quests.instruction: Find the word for someone who sits in class and does homework!
quests.question: Student
quests.hint: This person listens to the teacher and practices new skills.
quests.explanation: Well done! Every child in a classroom is a student, just like you.
quests.funFact: Being a good student means trying your best, even when something feels hard!

quests.instruction: Point to the stick that can be wiped away with a dry cloth!
quests.question: Chalk
quests.hint: It writes on a hard, dark board instead of on paper.
quests.explanation: Yes! Chalk is the stick we use to write on a blackboard.
quests.funFact: Outdoor chalk lets children draw colorful pictures right on the sidewalk!

quests.instruction: Find the box we open at lunchtime to eat our sandwich or fruit!
quests.question: Lunchbox
quests.hint: It usually has a lid or a zipper to keep food fresh.
quests.explanation: Well done! A lunchbox keeps a sandwich, fruit, or snack fresh and safe.
quests.funFact: Packing your own lunchbox can be a fun way to choose your favorite foods!

quests.instruction: Point to the item students use to write notes during a lesson!
quests.question: Notebook
quests.hint: It often has lines inside to help your writing stay neat.
quests.explanation: Correct! A notebook's pages are blank until a student fills them up.
quests.funFact: Writing in a notebook every day is a great way to practice new words!

quests.instruction: Find the tool that draws thick, colorful lines on paper or a board!
quests.question: Marker
quests.hint: If you leave its cap off too long, it can dry out.
quests.explanation: Well done! A marker's ink is thicker and darker than a pencil's.
quests.funFact: Some markers even smell like fruit, such as strawberry or grape!

quests.instruction: Point to the chart that helps us count down to a special day!
quests.question: Calendar
quests.hint: It has little boxes, one for each day of the month.
quests.explanation: Yes! A calendar shows the days, weeks, and months of the year.
quests.funFact: Some classroom calendars let students move a marker to show today's date!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool with a handle for each of your fingers!
quests.question: Scissors
quests.hint: You put your fingers in its handles and squeeze to make it cut.
quests.explanation: Correct! Scissors are always used slowly and carefully in the classroom.
quests.funFact: School scissors often have rounded tips to help keep little fingers safe!

quests.instruction: Point to the item that comes in little pots of many colors!
quests.question: Paint
quests.hint: It is wet and colorful until it dries on your paper.
quests.explanation: Yes! Paint is the colorful liquid we brush onto paper for art.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people made paint from crushed rocks, plants, and even berries!

quests.instruction: Touch the bag we wear on our shoulders to carry our school things!
quests.question: Backpack
quests.hint: You pack it in the morning and open it again after school.
quests.explanation: Yes! A backpack carries our books and supplies safely to and from school.
quests.funFact: Backpacks have two straps so the weight spreads evenly across both shoulders!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool that needs sharpening when its tip gets round!
quests.question: Pencil
quests.hint: You hold it between your fingers and press it gently on paper.
quests.explanation: Yes! A pencil is the tool we use to write words and draw pictures.
quests.funFact: The soft grey part inside a pencil is called graphite, not lead at all!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool that keeps many pages from falling apart!
quests.question: Stapler
quests.hint: It makes a little click sound when you press it down.
quests.explanation: Yes! A stapler presses a tiny metal pin through papers to hold them together.
quests.funFact: A stapler can join many sheets of paper together in just one press!

quests.instruction: Touch the thing full of pages and pictures that we read every day!
quests.question: Book
quests.hint: It can tell you a story about dragons, animals, or faraway places.
quests.explanation: Yes! A book is full of pages we read for stories and learning.
quests.funFact: The very first books were written by hand, long before printing was invented!

quests.instruction: Point to the bottle that lives in a side pocket of your backpack!
quests.question: Water Bottle
quests.hint: It is filled with water and often kept in your backpack.
quests.explanation: Yes! A water bottle holds water so we can drink during the school day.
quests.funFact: Many water bottles have a special cap so they never spill in a backpack!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool we twist open to stick our paper crafts together!
quests.question: Glue Stick
quests.hint: It helps two pieces of paper stay joined together, like magic!
quests.explanation: Yes! A glue stick makes paper sticky so our crafts stay together.
quests.funFact: Glue sticks were made so children could glue paper without sticky, messy fingers!

quests.instruction: Touch the little bag that keeps our pencils and erasers together!
quests.question: Pencil Case
quests.hint: It holds your pencils, eraser, and ruler all in one place.
quests.explanation: Yes! A pencil case keeps our pencils, erasers, and rulers together in one spot.
quests.funFact: Some pencil cases can stand up on their own like a little box!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool with soft bristles that spreads paint onto our paper!
quests.question: Paintbrush
quests.hint: You dip its bristles into paint before brushing it onto paper.
quests.explanation: That's right! We dip a paintbrush in paint before we brush a picture.
quests.funFact: Paintbrush bristles can be made from soft animal hair or from nylon!
